author: agent
objective: Estimate lag-specific rate ratios for daily COVID-19 hospital admissions among Sao Jose dos Campos residents per 10 ug/m3 O3 (lag 2) and NO2 (lag 3), using an ecological daily time-series negative-binomial model.

coverage_policy.evidence: The article gives no numeric completeness exclusion threshold; coverage will be reported, and analytic rows require nonmissing outcome, exposure and weather.

agent_design.research_question: Estimate lag-specific rate ratios for daily COVID-19 hospital admissions among Sao Jose dos Campos residents per 10 ug/m3 O3 (lag 2) and NO2 (lag 3), using an ecological daily time-series negative-binomial model.
agent_design.outcome: Daily count of COVID-19 hospital admissions of residents of Sao Jose dos Campos (article SIH-SUS target: ICD-10 B34.2).
agent_design.location_unit: Sao Jose dos Campos municipality (single city-level ecological series)
agent_design.principal_analysis_reference: Article Table 2: separate single-pollutant lag 0 through lag 7 negative-binomial models; co-primary reported contrasts are O3 lag 2 and NO2 lag 3.
agent_design.principal_effect_measure: Rate ratio exp(beta * 10) for a 10 ug/m3 increase, with 95% Wald confidence interval.
agent_design.representative_location_rule: Article-stated Sao Jose dos Campos coordinate, decimalized to latitude -23.1797, longitude -45.8872.
agent_design.monitor_distance_evidence: Article calls the CETESB data city-level but does not identify station; source-substituted coordinate model has no monitor distance. Representative coordinate is article's stated municipal location.
agent_design.exposure_metric: Daily arithmetic mean of hourly modeled/retrieved O3 and NO2 in ug/m3 at the city representative coordinate.
agent_design.daily_aggregation: Arithmetic mean of available hourly concentrations within each local calendar day.
agent_design.analysis_aggregation: Daily count outcome joined to pollutant value lagged 0 through 7 calendar days; principal outputs lag 2 O3 and lag 3 NO2.
agent_design.pollutant_combination: Separate single-pollutant models, matching the article Table 2 layout; no cross-pollutant combination.

design_evidence.outcome: article.txt lines 73-76: DATASUS SIH-SUS hospitalization records, ICD-10 B34.2; article.txt lines 34-36 gives dates.
design_evidence.exposure: article.txt lines 79-82: daily CETESB PM10, NO2 and O3 concentrations; city-level ecological time series.
design_evidence.model: article.txt lines 84-87: negative-binomial regression; lines 96-100: pollutants and weather with day-of-week and calendar-day control.
design_evidence.covariates: article.txt lines 79-82 and 96-98: temperature, relative humidity, day of week, calendar day.
design_evidence.published_estimate: article.txt lines 163-171 identifies O3 lag 2 and NO2 lag 3 as the reported primary lag-specific contrasts; no estimate was used in design choices.

coverage_policy.evidence: The article gives no numeric completeness exclusion threshold; coverage will be reported, and analytic rows require nonmissing outcome, exposure and weather.

agent_design.assignment_rule: Use the article's municipality-level support. Because a CETESB historical export currently requires login, use the municipal representative coordinate (article location coordinates, decimalized) with a transparent provider-model source substitution; do not call this personal exposure.
agent_design.aggregation_rule: Mean hourly source values by America/Sao_Paulo local calendar day; construct lags by date before joining to outcome counts.
agent_design.model: Negative-binomial GLM with log link; each pollutant-lag separately, adjusted for daily mean temperature, daily mean relative humidity, day-of-week indicators, and linear calendar-day trend.
agent_design.decision_rationale: The article defines an ecological municipality-level daily comparison. The retained single coordinate represents the city monitor/model location rather than individuals. No article-supported coverage threshold exists, so missingness is reported. The initial regulator portal probe showed authentication; the design therefore permits independently recovered public gridded data while preserving pollutant, unit, period, lags, contrast, and model family.
